layout_warnings: C7 (page 8) grid: text layer emits a single bare 'X' immediately after each row's factor label with NO column information; the mark's meaning is carried entirely by which of the four columns (Very Important / Important / Considered / Not Considered) it visually sits in. A naive linear text read will get every row's rating wrong or ambiguous. Confirmed by direct image inspection.

The same bare-X, column-position-carries-meaning hazard applies to every multi-column checkbox/radio grid in this range, not just C7: A2/A3/A4 (page 1, single-column so safe), C8A-C8G (page 9), D5 (page 13), D18 (page 14). These were NOT individually image-verified in this pass (budget reserved for C7 only) — treat any multi-column X grid in this document as unsafe to read from text order alone.

'D9' (page 13, D3-D11 section) is printed once per term row (Fall/Winter/Spring/Summer) in the transfer application-dates table, so the bare code 'D9' appears 4 times in the text stream. A naive extractor could mistake these for 4 distinct items or miss that they're all one grid.

B4-B21 (pages 4-6): the section heading 'B4-B21: Graduation Rates' appears only once, on page 4, but the individual CDS item codes B12 through B21 that belong to this same section do not appear in the text layer until page 6, three pages later. A page-routing heuristic keyed on individual item-code strings will misroute B12-B21 lookups away from page 4 (where the heading is) to page 6 (where the labels actually print), and will find no B4-B11 explicit label on any page — those rows are only identified by generic letters A-H plus the B4-B21 range heading.

'D12-D17: Transfer Credit Policies' subheading (page 14) is positioned in the PDF content stream AFTER the D12-D17 data rows it describes (text order: D11, D12, ... D17, then the heading text itself, then D18-D22 heading). Reading order does not match visual top-to-bottom order for this heading.

Table 2 on page 3 (B2, full/part-time by race/ethnicity) has its numeric grid and its row-label glossary (Nonresidents, Race/ethnicity unknown, Hispanic/Latino, Black or African American, White, American Indian/Alaska Native, Asian, Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander, Two or more races) printed as two separated blocks in the text stream, with instructional prose interleaved between them — row-to-number alignment cannot be done by naive proximity.

G1 (page 17) tuition/room/board table renders as an apparently all-blank skeleton in the plain text layer (no numeric values captured in reading order for Private/Public/All-Institution rows); this may be a genuine blank cell (Cornell often leaves G1 to a linked spreadsheet) or a text-extraction artifact from whitespace-positioned numbers — needs image spot-check if G1 values are needed downstream (out of scope for this 6-image budget).

text_layer_corruption.summary: No digit corruption observed anywhere in pages 1-17. Spot-checked the B1 gender/race enrollment table (e.g. 1,570 / 1,921 / 7,133 / 25,898 grand total), the C9 SAT/ACT percentile table (1470/1520/1550), and C7/C9 percentages (84.42%, 96.89%) — all render as clean, correctly-ordered digit strings. The only text-layer problems found are ORDERING/POSITION hazards (grid column ambiguity, heading-after-data ordering), not character-level digit corruption.

verdicts.header_year: The filename year (2022-2023) is CORRECT and matches the actual reported data. Evidence: (1) page 1's own running header reads 'Common Data Set 2022-2023', matching the filename, and is the header for the general-information/respondent section that would be filled in last/checked most carefully. (2) B1 enrollment counts are explicitly dated 'as of the institution's official fall reporting date or as of October 19, 2022' (page 3) — that is Fall 2022 data, i.e., a 2022-2023-cycle CDS. (3) C1/C9/F1 admissions and enrollment data are explicitly for 'Fall 2022' applicants/enrollees (pages 7, 9, 10, 16). (4) Page 4's graduation-rate instructions cite 'the IPEDS GRS Forms and Instructions for the 2022-2023 Survey.' (5) Section G (page 17) asks for '2023-2024 academic year' costs of attendance, which is exactly the forward-looking cost data a 2022-2023 CDS collects (CDS G-section costs are always for the upcoming academic year relative to the CDS cycle). CONCLUSION: pages 3 through 17 all carry a STALE, INCORRECT running header that says 'Common Data Set 2021-2022' — almost certainly because Cornell copied last year's template pages for sections B onward and never updated the running header text, while pages 1-2 (the A section, edited separately/more recently) got the correct header. Any page-routing or citation logic that trusts the per-page header string for pages 3-17 will mislabel the survey year; the header string must be ignored in favor of the filename/cover-page year for this document.
verdicts.c7_marker_semantics: Verified directly from the page 8 image. The mark is a plain typed capital 'X' (no checkmark glyph, no filled/shaded box — cells are open rectangles from a bordered table, and Cornell typed an 'X' character into exactly one cell per row). CRITICALLY: the mark itself carries NO information — every X on the page is visually identical. The meaning is carried ENTIRELY by which of the four columns (Very Important | Important | Considered | Not Considered) the X's cell falls under. Confirmed examples from the image: 'Rigor of secondary school record' -> X under Very Important; 'Class rank' -> X under Important (a different column than the row above it); 'Standardized test scores' -> X under Considered; 'Religious affiliation/commitment' -> X under Not Considered; 'Level of applicant's interest' -> X under Not Considered. The bare text layer (pymupdf get_text()) emits these as a flat sequence of row-label-then-'X' pairs with the four column header strings extracted separately at the top of the block and NO x/y-coordinate or column association carried through in plain reading order. THEREFORE: the text layer is UNUSABLE for recovering C7 (and by extension any same-shaped grid, see layout_warnings) — this grid must be read either from (a) word-level bounding-box coordinates (get_text('words') or get_text('dict') with column x-ranges) or (b) the rendered image, not from plain top-to-bottom/reading-order text extraction.

section_anchor_notes: Page 4: the phrase '(formerly CDS B4-B11)' appears twice in instructional prose (once describing the Pell/Stafford disaggregation groups, once in the note above the graduation-rate grid) — this is a PROSE reference to an old/retired CDS numbering scheme (item codes B4 through B11), not a section heading. A page-routing heuristic searching for literal 'B4' or 'B11' substrings would incorrectly anchor to page 4 for what is actually just an explanatory footnote about historical numbering; the live section heading on that page is 'B4-B21: Graduation Rates'.

Page 4: 'https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/use-the-data/survey-components/9/graduation-rates' and 'IPEDS Web-based Data Collection System's Graduation Rate Survey (GRS)' are external-system references, not CDS item codes, but could be mistaken for section anchors by a naive code-pattern matcher scanning for alphanumeric tokens near 'graduation'.

Page 12: 'C20 Common Application: Question removed from CDS. (Initiated during 2006-2007 cycle)' — C20 here IS the section's own heading/marker (legitimately anchors page 12), but the parenthetical '(Initiated during 2006-2007 cycle)' is prose that could be misread as another year/version reference if a heuristic is scanning for year-like tokens on this page.

Page 6: 'B22. Retention Rates' — note this is both used as the page's section heading label AND is immediately preceded on the same page by the tail end of the B4-B21 two-year-institution grid (B12-B21 labels); a heuristic anchoring purely on 'the last code seen' vs 'the first code seen' on page 6 would disagree about whether the page is 'about' B12-B21 or B22.
